name: Foscarnet
executiveSummary: Pyrophosphate analogue anti-herpes/CMV. Adult/pediatric CMV: induction **90 mg/kg every 12 h** or **60 mg/kg every 8 h**; maintenance **90–120 mg/kg/day**. Resistant HSV: **40 mg/kg every 8–12 h**. High nephrotoxicity — hydrate.
indications:
## Indications

- CMV retinitis/disease resistant or intolerant to ganciclovir.
- Acyclovir-resistant mucocutaneous HSV/VZV.

## Precautions

- Severe nephrotoxicity — pre/concomitant hydration; avoid other nephrotoxins.
- Ca/P/Mg disturbances; QT; seizures. High Na⁺ and phosphate content.
- Orientative max rate **60 mg/kg/h**.

> IV only. Adjust by creatinine per label.

adulto.dose: CMV induction: **90 mg/kg every 12 h** or **60 mg/kg every 8 h** × 14–21 days. Maintenance: **90–120 mg/kg every 24 h**. Resistant HSV: **40 mg/kg every 8–12 h**.
adulto.administration: Central: may run undiluted. Peripheral: dilute to ≤ **12 mg/mL** in NS/5% dextrose. Infuse **1–2 h** with pump. Hydrate with NS before/during.
adulto.notes: Each g provides ~10 mmol Na⁺ and ~3.3 mmol phosphate. Interactions: pentamidine (hypocalcemia), ciprofloxacin (seizures).

pediatrico.dose: Same per kg as adult: CMV induction **90 mg/kg every 12 h** or **60 mg/kg every 8 h**; maintenance **90–120 mg/kg/day**. Resistant HSV: **40 mg/kg every 8–12 h**.
pediatrico.administration: IV with pump; dilute if peripheral line.
pediatrico.notes: Monitor creatinine and electrolytes daily at the start.

neonatal.dose: ID only; not a routine neonatal regimen.

stability:
## Stability

- Do not refrigerate. Use per label after opening.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

AKI, hypo/hypercalcemia, hypo/hyperphosphatemia, hypomagnesemia, anemia, nausea, genital ulcers, seizures.
